scherrer_size — DRIVE pxrd op

• Data kinds: scalar × scalar × scalar → scalar

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.scherrer_size(fwhm, two_theta, wavelength, K=0.9, instrumental_fwhm=0.0, combine='gauss') (to call the implementation directly, import pxrd; pxrd.scherrer_size(fwhm, two_theta, wavelength, K=0.9, instrumental_fwhm=0.0, combine='gauss'); from the registry, opsdrive.get("scherrer_size"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Crystallite size [Å] by the Scherrer equation (L = K λ / (β cos θ)).

fwhm and instrumental_fwhm are full widths at half maximum in 2θ [deg], two_theta [deg], wavelength [Å]. The sample broadening β is combine="gauss" with sqrt(fwhm² − inst²) and "lorentz" with fwhm − inst. Passing arrays returns arrays. The Scherrer equation is a rough measure of the volume-weighted column length and does not distinguish strain broadening (proportional to tan θ) — when strain is suspected, look at the dependence on tan θ across multiple peaks, as in Williamson–Hall.

Raises ValueError: fwhm <= instrumental_fwhm (peak narrower than the instrument = size cannot be determined), non-positive values, misspellings.
